# **6 Best Rosie AI Alternatives in 2026**

We've talked to enough small business owners to know how this search starts. A booking flow seemed included, then turned out to sit on a pricier tier. A caller speaks a language the receptionist doesn't cover. Or the business outgrew a single phone line and now needs outbound reminders, CRM sync, and reporting.

We've been here too: once for a home services client that needed outbound reminders Rosie doesn't run, and once for a team juggling calls in three languages. Here's what matters: Rosie is an AI receptionist built for small businesses. It answers calls and, on its Scale plan, books appointments and handles live transfers.

Professional costs \$49/month for 250 minutes and takes messages only. Scale is \$149/month for 1,000 minutes, adding booking and live transfers. Growth runs \$299/month for 2,000 minutes, with a custom tier above that. Rosie offers a 7-day trial, covers English and Spanish, and doesn't run outbound calls.

The six alternatives below aim at something broader: voice-agent infrastructure, workflow automation, developer control, or documented compliance. That's a different category of tool. It's worth understanding the difference before comparing pricing pages.

## **How We Evaluated These Alternatives**

We started with each vendor's published pricing page and checked what's actually included. Published per-minute prices aren't directly comparable across platforms. Some bundle the model, transcription, and voice into one rate. Vapi instead charges a platform fee and passes provider costs through separately.

We compared the advertised rate against the likely cost of a real call. From there, we checked what compliance documentation each vendor actually provides. A landing-page badge and a signed report mean very different things during procurement. Where a certification wasn't independently verifiable, we flagged it as vendor-stated.

We also weighed realistic setup time against a scripted demo, since the two rarely match. Customer experiences were reviewed through G2 and Trustpilot, where current review data was available. Product capabilities, pricing, and compliance claims were checked against vendor documentation. Figures below come from published pricing and documentation, checked in September 2026\.

## **What Will These Platforms Actually Cost You?**

The effective cost depends on what each vendor bundles into its rate. Some fold the model, transcription, and voice into a single price, while others like Vapi charge a smaller platform fee but bill providers separately. For example, at 1,000 minutes/month, you could easily see \$50 in platform fees \+ \$20–\$50 in telephony \+ \$20–\$100 in AI/provider costs, putting the rough all-in cost at \$90–\$200/month.

Many platforms also charge separately for concurrency, phone numbers, transfers, and safety add-ons. Compare the full cost of a call, not just the headline platform price.

## **Best Rosie AI Alternatives for Different Use Cases**

### **Botphonic**

![][image2]  
![][image3]

Botphonic is a low-code AI call assistant that automates both inbound and outbound calls. It's built as a multi-channel platform, extending one agent across voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and email, rather than treating each channel as a separate build. Pricing runs pay-as-you-go, roughly \$0.15 to \$0.40 per minute. New accounts can test the platform before committing, with current trial terms shown at signup.

**Best for:** Businesses that want one agent running across voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and email without rebuilding logic per channel. 

**Rating:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.8/5 on G2

**What Stands Out:**

* **CRM updates during the workflow:** Calls can update Salesforce, HubSpot, or Zoho records, so information captured by the agent can flow directly into the CRM.  
* **SIP and existing-number support:** Businesses can connect existing phone infrastructure through SIP providers such as Twilio, Telnyx, and Plivo instead of necessarily replacing their current numbers.  
* **Branded outbound caller ID:** Lists branded caller ID for outbound campaigns, helping businesses present a recognizable calling identity rather than relying on an unfamiliar number.  
* **Payment-reminder workflows:** Outbound agents can be used for payment reminders, giving businesses a use case beyond sales and appointment follow-up.  
* **Multichannel automation:** The platform extends beyond voice into SMS, WhatsApp, and email, allowing follow-up to continue after the phone conversation.

| Pros: Useful for businesses fielding the same customer across multiple channels. Guided onboarding can shorten the setup process for a first agent. Pay-as-you-go pricing avoids paying for unused monthly minutes. CRM write-back is native rather than routed through a third-party connector. ### **Synthflow AI**

![][image4]

Synthflow is a no-code, drag-and-drop voice agent builder. However, the platform has eliminated its public self-serve pay-as-you-go tiers and free trials. Instead, access is strictly sales-led via custom Enterprise contracts that require a minimum commitment starting at \$30,000 per year. While the core voice engine still costs approximately \$0.09/minute and LLMs cost \$0.02–\$0.05/minute, you can no longer sign up on a simple per-minute basis without an upfront annual contract.

* **Enterprise capacity planning.** Current pricing is based on expected volume, concurrency, telephony, integrations, security requirements, and launch support, rather than a single universal per-minute rate.

### **Vapi**

![][image5]

Vapi is an orchestration layer that connects your own language model, transcription provider, voice, and telephony into one real-time call through an API. Its pricing calculator provides con figuration-dependent estimates, so the final per-minute cost depends on the providers and components selected, and the platform fee doesn't include provider costs. It's built for teams that want to own the stack rather than take a packaged agent.

**Best for:** Engineering teams that want full control over the model stack and are comfortable managing separate provider costs.

**Rating:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.2/5 on G2

**What Stands Out:**

* **Component-level control.** Vapi allows teams to choose and operate their own models, transcription providers, voices, and other components rather than locking the entire application to one packaged stack.  
* **Transparent provider economics.** Vapi states that provider costs are passed through without markup, while its own hosting fee is charged separately.  
* **Testing and simulation.** Teams can simulate calls before exposing an agent to customers, which is particularly useful when workflows contain multiple branches or tool calls.	

| Pros: New accounts get \$5 in free credits.  Component-level pricing transparency makes cost modeling easier. Strong fit for teams that already have engineering resources in place. ### **Bland AI**

![][image6]

Bland is an API-first platform built around Pathways, its node-based visual builder. It states its core AI stack runs on its own infrastructure, reducing reliance on third-party models. Pricing runs \$0.14/minute on Start, or \$0.12/minute plus \$299/month on Build; Enterprise is custom. Transfer minutes bill separately at \$0.05 and \$0.04.

**Best for:** Teams in regulated industries that need documented compliance controls and developer-oriented voice workflows.

**Rating:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5/5 on G2

**What Stands Out:**

* **Fully loaded per-minute pricing.** Bland says its per-minute rate includes the language model, speech recognition, and speech synthesis, making the headline usage price easier to interpret than a platform fee that excludes provider costs.  
* **Pathways visual builder.** Developers can create branching call logic, API calls, knowledge-base lookups, authentication steps, and other actions through Bland's workflow tooling.  
* **Published volume limits.** The Start plan supports 100 calls per day and 10 concurrent calls, while Build increases those limits to 2,000 calls per day and 50 concurrent calls.

| Pros: 40+ languages on its own transcription model Native scheduling and SMS nodes built into the call flow The Start plan includes credits and an inbound number valued at \$15/month, with no card required. ## **How to Choose the Right Alternative**

Start with the call, not the feature table. A simple message-taking flow and a branching conversation need different tools. A platform built for one will frustrate you on the other.

Price it against real volume, not pilot volume. A trial always looks affordable; a few thousand monthly calls tell a different story. See "What Will This Actually Cost You?" above for what's typically billed outside the headline rate.

Ask for the underlying compliance documentation, not just the badge. A BAA is an important contractual requirement when applicable, but it does not by itself establish that the overall implementation is HIPAA compliant.

Read the latency claim as a claim. Every vendor publishes a number, and no two are measured the same way. The most useful test is your own call, on your own phone and telephony.

## **Find the Right Rosie AI Alternative**

Rosie is designed for straightforward requirements such as answering inbound calls, taking messages, booking appointments, and routing callers. The alternatives become more relevant when the business needs the AI to handle more of the customer journey.

The biggest difference is often what the AI can do beyond the phone call. CRM updates, calendar actions, SMS follow-ups, API connections, and human handoffs can turn a voice agent from a virtual receptionist into an operational tool.

For that broader use case, Botphonic is particularly worth considering. It combines inbound and outbound calling with 50+ languages, calendar booking, CRM integrations, SIP connectivity, and SMS, WhatsApp, and email workflows. That makes it a closer fit for businesses looking to automate more than their front desk.

The best next step is to test the platforms against the calls your business actually receives. A short pilot can quickly show whether the agent understands your customers, follows your workflows, and handles the edge cases that matter.

## **FAQs**

### **Is Rosie AI still suitable for small businesses?**

For a solo owner needing inbound calls, messages, booking, and transfers, Rosie may cover the basics. The gaps: languages beyond English and Spanish, outbound calling, deeper automation, and developer-level control.

### **What is the cheapest Rosie alternative?**

There isn't a meaningful cheapest option based on headline per-minute pricing alone. Vapi's \$0.05/minute fee is the lowest listed here, but excludes provider costs. Retell runs \$0.07–\$0.31, Botphonic \$0.15–\$0.40, and Bland \$0.14 on Start. Synthflow and Cresta are sales-led, so compare full call cost before calling anything "cheaper."

### **Which Rosie alternatives support multiple languages?**

Five list fixed counts; Vapi's depends on your providers. Retell lists 55+, Botphonic and Synthflow 50+, Bland 40+, and Cresta 30+. Vapi's coverage depends on the transcription and voice providers you connect. Match the count to the languages your callers actually speak, rather than defaulting to the highest number.

### **Can Rosie alternatives make outbound calls?**

Five of six list outbound calling, though workflows and limits differ. Cresta's public materials focus on inbound, so confirm outbound support directly. Bland's Start plan caps at 100 calls/day, so larger campaigns may need Build or above. If outbound volume matters to you, check each plan's daily cap and concurrency limit before committing.

### **Do I need developers to switch?**

Not always. Botphonic, Synthflow, and Cresta's Receptionist use plain-language, non-technical setup. Vapi, Bland, and Retell expect developer involvement.

### **Do we need HIPAA compliance if we're not in healthcare?**

[HIPAA obligations](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/index.html) apply to covered entities and business associates when they handle protected health information in covered activities. Whether your business falls into either category depends on the services and data involved. 

### **How long does a realistic switch from Rosie AI actually take?**

It depends on call flow complexity, integrations, telephony, and testing. A simple no-code setup may take days; a developer-led build takes longer. Budget extra time for compliance if you're in a regulated industry. Bland's own 28-day enterprise onboarding is a useful reference point.
